paper_title: Learning Partitions with Optimal Query and Round Complexities
authors: Hadley Black, Arya Mazumdar, Barna Saha
statement: We are interested in the query complexity of learning partitions when an upper bound of s ∈ [2, n] is placed on the allowed size of a queried subset. Strong queries are the most informative type of subset query that one can define for the partition learning problem and thus provide a meaningful benchmark against which to measure the effectiveness of other query types. When s = 2, both queries are equivalent (in fact they are the same as pairwise queries). At the other extreme, when s = n a single strong query recovers the entire partition, while a weak query only returns the number of parts. Intuitively, as s increases, the gap between weak and strong queries widens. Given that weak queries require significantly less communication from the oracle (O(log k) as opposed to O(s log k) bits), as well as less computation to answer, a motivating question for this line of inquiry is: is there a regime of s ≫ 2 where weak and strong queries are similarly powerful? The non-adaptive case. Obtaining lower bounds, even for strong subset queries, is straightforward using known lower bounds for pairwise queries: observe that one s-bounded strong subset query can be simulated (non-adaptively) by 2s pair-wise same-set queries3 . Thus, for non-adaptive algorithms, the Ω(n2 ) lower bound for pairwise queries Mazumdar and Saha (2017a); Black et al. (2024) implies that Ω(n2 /s2 ) strong queries are necessary. In fact, we prove (in Section D) that there is also a simple deterministic non-adaptive algorithm matching this bound.
context: 2.1. Subset Queries Next, we consider the two following generalizations of pairwise same-set queries to subsets. Given hidden partition P and a queried subset S ⊆ U , each oracle returns the following information. P • Weak subset query oracle: Given S ⊆ U , the oracle returns count(S, P) := X∈P 1(S ∩ X ̸= ∅), i.e. the number of parts which S intersects.2 • Strong subset query oracle: Given S ⊆ U , the oracle returns partition(S, P) := {S ∩ X : X ∈ P}, i.e. a full description of P restricted on S.
